name: Heron: Website Change Monitor
summary: Get told when a web page changes. Watch a whole page or just one part, like a price or a stock notice, and see what was added and removed. Every check runs in your browser: no account, no cloud, no paid plan. Free, no ads, no tracking.
description:
Heron watches web pages for you and tells you when they change: a price, a stock notice, a news page, a timetable, a job board, release notes.

**Watch**
- A whole page, or one part of it: click the part on the page and Heron watches just that
- Checks run in the background on the schedule you set for each watch, from every 5 minutes to once a week
- Pause, resume or check any watch right now
- Add pages from the toolbar button, or by address

**See what changed**
- A number on the toolbar button shows how many watches have something new
- The change view shows what was added and what was removed, down to the words inside an edited line
- The last 10 versions of each watch are kept, so you can look back
- Optional desktop notifications, off until you switch them on

**Everything stays in your browser**
- No account, no server, no cloud: fetching, comparing and storing all happen on your device
- Nothing is uploaded. The only requests Heron makes go straight to the pages you watch
- Export and import your watch list as a file

**Free, for real**
Every feature is unlocked for everyone: no paid plan and no quota of checks. No ads, no account, no analytics.

If Heron saves you checking pages by hand and you'd like to say thanks, there's a Ko-fi link in the popup. It's entirely optional and unlocks nothing.

**Permissions**
Heron asks for no access to your websites when you install it. When you add a watch, Firefox asks you to let Heron read that one site and nothing else. Delete the last watch for a site and Heron gives that access back.

**Good to know**
- Heron reads the HTML a site's server sends, without opening the page. Parts that a page draws later with JavaScript can't be seen that way. If you pick such a part, Heron tells you right away instead of silently watching nothing
- Checks are made without your cookies, so Heron sees what a signed-out visitor sees. Pages behind a sign-in can't be watched. This is on purpose: a background check can never act on your account, and private pages never end up in the saved versions
- Text is compared. A change in pictures or layout alone is not reported
- Checks run while Firefox is open. Missed ones are caught up when it starts
- The shortest interval is 5 minutes, to be gentle on the sites you watch. Up to 200 watches
- Desktop Firefox only for now: it could not be tested on Firefox for Android, so it is not offered there
